subject: Optimize toolkit: pricing & packaging tradeoffs for Hyperscale pilot (batching/caching/quant)
messages:
From: Linda Gomez <linda@hyperscale.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial pricing & packaging ask for Optimize toolkit pilot

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Hyperscale infra team and I have been chewing on the Optimize toolkit capabilities. We're planning a ~90-day pilot that will exercise heavy inference: roughly 100M model tokens/month across a mix of short (<64 tokens) and medium (64-512) completions, 99th-pct latency target ~350ms for our interactive routing layer.

High-level asks:
- Can you map pricing/packaging options for hosted vs dedicated for a pilot of this size?
- We want to understand the economics of batching and KV caching (how you credit savings or apply discounts).
- Would Redwood include a quantization assessment (Llama-like models -> 8-bit/4-bit guidance) as part of pilot credits or is that a separate engagement?

I've attached a lightweight infra overview (hyperscale-infra-overview.pdf) that shows our region split and expected peak QPS. Procurement will want a sketch of commercial options to evaluate against their vendor matrix.

Appreciate a short commercial sketch and whether you can do a one-off quant assessment.

Thanks,
Linda
Linda Gomez
Head of Platform
Hyperscale.ai

Attachment: hyperscale-infra-overview.pdf (1 page PDF, infra summary)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Linda Gomez <linda@hyperscale.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial pricing & packaging ask for Optimize toolkit pilot

Hi Linda — great to hear from you and thanks for the overview.

Short answer: yes, we can both structure a pilot with targeted credits for batching/KV cache and include a complimentary quantization assessment for the set of model families you intend to use. Below is a concise commercial sketch and options so procurement can get a sense quickly.

Pilot commercial sketch (90 days):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): baseline per-token price + 1x free KV cache trial credit bucket (applies to first 30 days or 10M cached tokens, whichever comes first).
- Pilot commit (recommended for predictable economics): $50k commit for 3 months, tiered unit pricing that applies after credit consumption. Includes 25 hours of Redwood ops support and a quantization assessment (report + recommended quant profiles).
- Dedicated evaluation (short-term reserved pool): for deterministic latency at scale — requires a minimum commitment; we can present pricing if you expect sustained peak QPS across regions.

How we handle batching/caching discounts and credits:
- KV cache credits: we provide a credit bucket that offsets billed inference tokens equal to observed cache hits (with conservative hit-to-savings mapping).
- Batching guidance: optimization suggestions and runtime parameter tweaks. We typically do not discount purely for batching, but for pilot commits we apply a unit price that reflects expected batching benefits.

Quantization assessment: complimentary for pilots > $50k commit. It includes a short bench (latency, accuracy lift/loss) and a recommended quant profile map for each model family. Full on-prem quantization work would be scoped separately.

Next steps I propose:
1) We prepare a one-page pilot SOW + commercial sketch (attached).
2) Product runs an initial ops checklist (sample token profile + latency SLO) — cc'd Stephanie and Connor who can follow up on technical constraints.
3) Schedule a 30min commercial + ops sync (I can propose times).

I've attached a two-pager (pilot-commercial-sketch.pdf) and a short explainer on KV cache credits (kvcache-credit-explainer.md).

Would tomorrow at 10am PT work for a quick sync?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pilot-commercial-sketch.pdf, kvcache-credit-explainer.md

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Linda Gomez <linda@hyperscale.ai>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial pricing & packaging ask for Optimize toolkit pilot

Hi Linda — thanks for looping us in. A few technical clarifications that will help scope credits and the quant assessment accurately:

1) Token length distribution: can you share approximate percentiles (p50, p90, p99) and how often you hit 512+ sequences?
2) Latency SLO: you noted 99th ~350ms — is that wall-clock including network hops to our hosted endpoint, or is it purely server-side?
3) Batching tolerance: what fraction of requests can tolerate 40–120ms extra wait to enable larger batch formation? This impacts expected batching efficiency and the unit economics we model for pricing.
4) Quant sensitivity: do you have internal accuracy thresholds (e.g., top-1/semantic drift allowance) where we should avoid lower-bit quant?

Operational guardrails we usually recommend for pilots:
- Canary traffic routing (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic fallback to baseline model family.
- Budget alerting and pre-emptive throttle thresholds to avoid surprise overages.

If you can drop a small sample of production traces (anonymized), we can produce a short cost-savings sketch that maps to your token profile. Connor — can you capture runbook snippets (alert thresholds, rollback steps) for the SOW?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Product, Optimize Toolkit
Redwood Inference

From: Linda Gomez <linda@hyperscale.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@hyperscale.ai, sam.yao@hyperscale.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial pricing & packaging ask for Optimize toolkit pilot

Vanessa / Stephanie — thanks for the fast replies. Answers inline below: 

1) Token profile: p50 ~ 48 tokens, p90 ~ 340 tokens, p99 ~ 900 tokens. ~12% of requests exceed 512 tokens (those are batch-extraction jobs).
2) Latency SLO: the 350ms target is end-to-end from our edge -> Redwood hosted endpoint -> back to edge. Server-side budget should be <= 250ms to accommodate network.
3) Batching tolerance: about 60% of traffic can tolerate an extra 40ms for batching, the rest is interactive and needs sub-200ms additional wait.
4) Quant sensitivity: we can tolerate up to ~2% semantic drift on low-importance completions (logging/formatting), but core ranking/inference must be within 0.5% of baseline.

I've attached an anonymized token-profile.csv and our procurement lead is copied for commercial follow-up. Tomorrow 10am PT works for the call. Procurement may ask to see a short pilot SOW and a redlineable MSA.

Appreciate the concrete sketch.

Regards,
Linda

Attachment: token-profile.csv
